messages:
sarah: Quick check — prepping a provable isolation rollout for private/on‑prem installs. Goal: shrink RBAC for provisioning, lock egress to a KMS proxy or customer's KMS, and enable signed audit forwarding. Any obvious gaps?

matt: SGTM. Suggest staged canary: 2 tenants in staging -> 1 prod shard -> full roll. Need netpols for sidecars/metrics before RBAC shrink so observability stays intact.

jenny: Also flagging a vuln: keystore-agent v1.2.0 has CVE-2025-1234 (privilege escalation in listener). Patch to v1.2.3 first. That might require short maintenance window for the canary nodes.

sarah: Good catch. Plan: 1) patch keystore-agent in canary 2) enable audit-level=debug for 24h, ship signed logs to secure S3 3) shrink clusterrole for node-provisioner 4) rotate wrapping keys after success.

matt: Example RBAC patch I'll run in staging (one-liner):
```bash
kubectl patch clusterrole node-provisioner -p '{"rules":[{"apiGroups":[""],"resources":["pods","secrets"],"verbs":["get","list","watch"]}]}'
```
Confirming: this removes broad write perms but keeps read for health checks.

nate: Netpol template for deny-by-default egress (allow only kms-proxy + prometheus):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-kms-proxy
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/24 # prometheus/monitoring
```
Will validate CIDRs per-customer.

jenny: Audit/logging question: we need logs signed using an HSM-backed wrapping key before leaving the cluster. For private with customer KMS, do we expect them to provide an endpoint that accepts signing requests, or do we run a local connector?

sarah: We support both modes. For customer-managed KMS we require an allowlist entry to their KMS host + mTLS to the key endpoint. For airgapped HSMs we ship a local connector that signs via the HSM agent. Documented in the runbook: https://intranet/docs/priv-deploy/kms-integration (I'll add a step-by-step for the canary).

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-045 for keystore-agent upgrade tracking (assigned: jenny).

nate: Operationally we should add an egress-spike detector that triggers node-quarantine if unexpected KMS targets are contacted. That helps with provable isolation metrics.

jenny: I'll add a short checklist to the playbook: [patch agent, apply netpol, reduce RBAC, enable signed audit forwarder, KMS allowlist & mTLS, rotate wrap keys, run canary, monitor egress & audit logs].

sarah: Scheduling the canary for tonight 22:00 PT. Tagging @matt @jenny @nate — please reply +1 if you can be on call.

matt: +1 :thumbsup:

jenny: +1, prepping runbook updates and rollback steps.

sarah: Thanks — will post postmortem template if anything odd shows up.
